env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

[!race] skip 'the platform has no race detector'
[!cgo] skip 'the race runtime links through cgo'
[!GOOS:linux] [!GOOS:darwin] [!GOOS:freebsd] skip 'plugin cgo paths exist only on linux, darwin and freebsd'

env CC=
env CGO_ENABLED=

cd forbid

# A standard-library cgo package is exempt from the ban, even in a raced
# build: the policy applies to LoGOs main modules only, so plugin links.
logos build -race .
logos run -race main.lgo

# The raced build selects the cgo plugin implementation, not the stub.
[!GOOS:darwin] logos list -race -f '{{.CgoFiles}}' plugin
[!GOOS:darwin] stdout 'dlopen'
# Without -race the stub is selected, so the assertion above discriminates.
logos list -f '{{.CgoFiles}}' plugin
! stdout 'dlopen'

# Without -race no C sources enter the build, so the stubs link normally.
logos build .

# The race runtime linkage itself still works under the ban.
! logos test -race -count=1 ./racy
stdout 'WARNING: DATA RACE'
! stderr 'requires cgo'

-- forbid/go.mod --
module example.com/forbidstd

go 1.27

-- forbid/logos.toml --
[build]
cgo = "forbid"

-- forbid/main.lgo --
package main

import _ "plugin"

func main() {}

-- forbid/racy/racy.lgo --
package racy

import (
	"context"
	"sync"
)

func Count(ctx context.Context) (int, error) {
	n := 0
	var start sync.WaitGroup
	start.Add(1)
	go group (ctx) {
		go {
			start.Wait()
			for i := 0; i < 1000; i++ {
				n++
			}
		}
		go {
			start.Wait()
			for i := 0; i < 1000; i++ {
				n++
			}
		}
		start.Done()
	}
	return n, nil
}

-- forbid/racy/racy_test.lgo --
package racy

import (
	"context"
	"testing"
)

func TestCount(t *testing.T) {
	if _, err := Count(context.Background()); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}
